solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hearts facing foremost of overseas clubs — important game

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: foremost means the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the opening letter of overseas
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs
key as an adjective means crucial or important

explanation.surface: A football report: Hearts take on the best of the foreign clubs in a big match.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts and clubs look like football teams (Hearts is a Scottish club) but are card suits, each giving its one-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hockey is a team sport played with sticks and a ball or puck, so it is one kind of game.

clue.text: Anglo-Saxon leader in this place on a charge

parts.note: here means in this place
a ward is someone placed in another's charge

explanation.surface: A Saxon chieftain stands here accused of some offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a charge' reads as being accused, but a charge is a person in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward the Wake led English resistance against the Norman conquerors in the Fens after 1066.

clue.text: Queen's absurd charade wore thin

indicators.note: something absurd makes no sense as it stands, so the following words must be rearranged

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The queen's silly pretence started to lose its credibility.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Howard was the fifth wife of Henry VIII and so an English queen consort, later beheaded.

clue.text: Public school board losing leader

indicators.note: losing its leader means the word drops its opening letter

parts.note: to board a bus or train is to get on it

explanation.surface: A private school's governing board loses its chairman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School board' reads as one committee, but board is a verb here: get on, which without its G leaves ETON.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the most famous of England's fee-paying schools, which the British confusingly call public schools.

clue.text: Fine work of art, attractive

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an etching is a print made from an engraved plate

explanation.surface: An art critic praises a fine and attractive piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching describes someone or something charming and pleasing to look at, a close synonym.

clue.text: Girl one earl abused

indicators.note: abused means mistreated or misused, so the words are knocked out of their proper order

parts.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A grim tale of a young woman mistreated by an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a female first name, and crosswords use girl to define any woman's name.

clue.text: Commanding Officer at a drugs bust?

definitions.text: Commanding Officer at a drugs bust?

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for commanding officer

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the preceding letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An officer in charge leads a raid on smugglers bringing narcotics ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition; the question mark admits the description is a fanciful one.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastguards patrol shores and coastal waters, and intercepting smuggled narcotics is part of their work.

clue.text: Then I exercised, completely naked

indicators.note: exercised means stirred up or agitated, so those words are jumbled

parts.note: five letters to rearrange
altogether means entirely or completely

explanation.surface: After a workout someone stands without a stitch of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Exercised suggests a gym session, which suits the nakedness, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the altogether' is a humorous British expression for wearing no clothes at all.

clue.text: Earl entering courtyard with a Knight of the Round Table

definitions.text: a Knight of the Round Table

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a garth is an enclosed courtyard, as in a cloister
E is an abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A nobleman walks into the castle yard alongside one of Arthur's knights.
explanation.walkthrough: Garth is an old word for a yard or garden enclosed by buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gareth is one of King Arthur's knights in Malory's Morte d'Arthur, brother of Gawain.

clue.text: Bird pecking a rook in overcrowded place

indicators.note: a bird pecking holds things in its beak, so it takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: a wren is a small songbird
taken as written
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: One bird attacks another in a cramped nesting site.
explanation.walkthrough: Rook looks like the bird; it is the chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren, literally a network of rabbit burrows, is figuratively any cramped, densely packed building or district.

clue.text: Limit beer in grounds

parts.note: to ration is to limit the amount allowed
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A rule restricting drinking on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: Grounds looks like the premises where beer is banned, but it means reasons.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning or justification for something, just as grounds are reasons for an action.

clue.text: Become different later, when drunk

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about out of order, so the word's letters are muddled

parts.note: five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A person's character changes later in the evening after drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter, used intransitively, means to change, which is to become different from before.

clue.text: Duke on very small inferior horse

indicators.note: in a down-style reading the duke sits on top, so here it follows, placed after the other piece

parts.note: wee is a Scottish word for very small
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: An aristocrat rides a tiny, poor-quality pony.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the duke first, but 'on' puts him after the other piece, sitting on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A weed, besides a garden pest, can mean a weak, worthless animal, especially a feeble racehorse.

clue.text: Type of crime exposed by marvellous newpaper!

parts.note: grand can mean splendid or marvellous
THE FT, the Financial Times, this crossword's own newspaper

explanation.surface: A splendid paper breaks the story of a criminal scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, which printed this puzzle; the exclamation mark winks at that.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand theft is a legal category, in the US especially, for stealing property above a set value.

clue.text: PA a fellow uses in resort

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again into a new order

parts.note: a fellow is a man
six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man employs an assistant while staying at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a seaside town, but split as re-sort it orders a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a literary assistant who takes dictation or copies manuscripts, much like a personal assistant.

clue.text: Film of artist, US portrait painter

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stand-in for an artist
Henry Inman was a nineteenth-century American portraitist

explanation.surface: A movie about one artist made by an American portraitist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain Man is the 1988 Oscar-winning movie starring Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise.

clue.text: Difficulty disposing of capital, Ivan's money?

indicators.note: capital here is the opening capital letter, which is to be thrown away

parts.note: trouble is difficulty

explanation.surface: A Russian named Ivan struggles to spend his savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money, which fits the surface, but it is the first letter. Ivan stands for any Russian, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is Russia's currency, so it is the cash a typical Russian such as Ivan would spend.

clue.text: Knife fight involving upset drunk

indicators.note: involving means including, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or scrap

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out involving an angry drunk with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a dagger with a narrow, tapering blade, so it is a type of knife.

clue.text: Nine injured in extremely treacherous sport

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
extremely means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of treacherous

indicators.note: something injured is damaged or bent out of shape, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Nine players are hurt in a dangerous game.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net on a court, one example of a sport.

clue.text: One moves off quickly in vehicle

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who scoots, or dashes away
second meaning: a small motorbike or a child's kick-board with handlebars

explanation.surface: Someone makes a quick getaway in a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoot is to dart off, so a scooter is one who does so; it is also a small motorised two-wheeler.

clue.text: Review involving Royal Marines over in a US state

indicators.note: involving means including, so the first piece wraps around what follows

parts.note: to vet is to review or check closely
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marines
on can mean over, as in a lid on a box

explanation.surface: An inspection of British marine commandos taking place in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Over looks like a reversal signal; here it simply means on top of.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is a New England state in the northeastern United States, bordering Canada.

clue.text: Primate showing spirit? Tons

parts.note: verve is energy or spirit
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A lively monkey displays tons of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The vervet is a small African monkey, and monkeys belong to the primate order of mammals.

clue.text: Type of sausage obtained from one of the Greek islands, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is left off

parts.note: Salamis is a Greek island near Athens, site of a famous sea battle

explanation.surface: A sausage brought over from a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured, highly seasoned Italian sausage usually eaten in thin slices.

clue.text: More get on without deception

parts.note: above means more than, as in above the limit
to get on a ship or train is to board it

explanation.surface: Advice to get along better while staying honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means open and legitimate, the idiom for dealings conducted honestly and frankly.

clue.text: Fortunate? Quite possibly

explanation.walkthrough: The two question-and-answer phrases read as a brief exchange about luck, but each is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb and adjective cover both luckiness, as in 'just as well', and likelihood, as in 'might well happen'.

clue.text: Regret about daughter being bad-mannered

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes around the next

parts.note: to rue is to regret
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent laments a daughter's impolite behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude describes someone impolite or discourteous, a direct synonym for lacking good manners.

clue.text: Gather a large amount

parts.note: taken as written
a mass is a large quantity

explanation.surface: Collect a great deal of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one plain instruction, but it splits after the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or accumulate, especially a large quantity over time.

clue.text: Monstrous brute caught the wild type of onager

indicators.note: monstrous suggests something grotesquely misshapen, so the word that follows is distorted
wild means out of control, so the preceding letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: A savage beast traps a wild ass.
explanation.walkthrough: An onager is a wild ass, which the surface plays on, but it is also an ancient stone-throwing siege engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A trebuchet is a medieval siege catapult, and the onager is a related torsion-powered stone thrower.

clue.text: Attempt to go after Asian river trade

indicators.note: going after means following, so that piece is placed second

parts.note: the Indus flows through Pakistan
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Merchants try to follow an Asian river to do business.
explanation.definitionFit: Industry and trade both name commercial and manufacturing activity as a whole, as in 'trade and industry'.

clue.text: I rowed out to identify queer fish

indicators.note: out can mean out of order or awry, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone rows out on the water to spot an odd-looking fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Queer fish sounds like a catch from the boat; it is an idiom for an eccentric person.
explanation.definitionFit: A queer fish is a dated British idiom for a strange or eccentric person, which is what a weirdo is.
